sector: Volunteer run community road running club with its own spring race, printing kit and race bibs for its members.
founded_place_size: Founded 1994 by Del in Providence, Rhode Island. A volunteer run club with roughly thirty eight members on the books.
about: Ironway Run Club is a volunteer community running club in Providence with about thirty eight members. Its identity is the numbering the founder drew by hand in 1994, which the members treat as the club itself, and a screen printed club mark that survives on an old singlet. Each spring the kit goes to the heat transfer shop and every member runs the club's own Founders Five race with a bib.
audience: Members aged roughly 22 to 68, half of whom pin a bib on in the dark before a wet April race. Volunteers, not customers.
price_positioning: A forty dollar per season volunteer club with no sponsor. Everything printed must be cheap at volume and survive weather: one colour throughout, nothing that adds a plate or a pass, and nothing that looks like a paid entry event.

palette.name: Rail Navy
palette.role: mandatory: the one ink on every bib and the one colour of the club mark
palette.usage: Everything printed on a bib, the drawn number, club mark, club name, member name and details, on Bib White, as on ironway_bib_2025.pdf; the single colour of club-mark.svg, the navy the mark is printed in on ironway_singlet_mark.jpg; one of the two allowed fills for a glyph master. It is also the colour of the new singlet in ironway_kit_swatch.jpg.

palette.name: Bib White
palette.role: mandatory on every bib, as the ground only
palette.usage: The paper ground of every bib, as on ironway_bib_2025.pdf. Never an ink: nothing is printed in it, and no glyph master or club mark is drawn in it.

palette.name: Marshal Orange
palette.role: optional: cut film and glyph masters only
palette.usage: The shop's stock Marshal Orange transfer film, the one flat colour the numbers and club letters are cut in and pressed onto the Rail Navy singlet, as ironway_kit_shop_note.txt and the chip on ironway_kit_swatch.jpg show; one of the two allowed fills for a glyph master. Never on a bib or the club mark.

palette.name: Iron Grey
palette.usage: Not an ink on any commissioned file: no bib, glyph master or club mark uses it, since each prints in one ink. It may appear only in supporting previews, which the brief welcomes but which cannot replace the named files.

typography: Ironway keeps the founder's hand at the top of the scale. The bib numeral is Del's 1994 hand drawn numbering at 120 pt on 126 pt, spacing taken off the original sheet, and it is never set in Antwerp. Directly above it sits the club name in Antwerp Bold caps at 14 pt on 16 pt, tracking +0.08 em, which is the near nine to one jump the club is recognised by; Antwerp Bold also carries race titles, and Antwerp Bold Italic is reserved for the race year and nothing else. Member names are Benton Sans Bold at 24 pt on 27 pt. Details and body run in Benton Sans Regular at 10 pt on 13 pt, tracking 0, held to 65 characters a line, and fine print in Benton Sans Regular at 8 pt on 11 pt, tracking +0.04 em. One ink throughout.
voice: Friendly, plain, volunteer to volunteer. A line the club would write: "Founders Five is on. Pin your bib, mind the puddles, we will see you at the line."
brand_assets_status: No digital brand files exist. The numbering survives only as a phone photograph of the founder's original ink sheet on drafting paper, and the club mark only as a photograph of it screen printed on an old singlet. Nobody knows who made the mark and there is no file of either. Last year's bib survives as the printer's returned press PDF.
values: The founder's hand is the club, so it is kept faithfully. Legible beats clever, and every member gets the same thing for their forty dollars.

Italic is reserved for the race year and nothing else.
One ink throughout. Nothing that adds a plate or a pass, and nothing that looks like a paid entry event.

palette_rules.distribution: Every commissioned file uses exactly one ink. Each bib is Rail Navy on a Bib White ground and nothing else, as on ironway_bib_2025.pdf: the drawn number, club mark, club name, member name and details are all Rail Navy. club-mark.svg is Rail Navy alone on a transparent ground. Each numeral and letter master is one flat fill, Rail Navy or Marshal Orange, on a transparent ground. Marshal Orange is the kit film on the Rail Navy singlet and never prints on a bib. Iron Grey appears only in supporting previews.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, screen, halftone, transparency, gradient, shadow, outline or blend mode is applied to any colour on a bib, the club mark or a glyph, and no photograph, scan or raster image is placed on a bib: the club mark is the delivered vector, never the raster photograph of the singlet mark placed at the head of ironway_bib_2025.pdf.
palette_rules.forbidden: No second ink on any file: no Marshal Orange, Iron Grey or other colour on a bib, and no second colour, outline, shade or keyline on a glyph or the club mark, which ironway_kit_shop_note.txt allows as one flat shape only. No colour outside the four palette hexes.
palette_rules.photography: No photograph appears in any delivered file. ironway_numbering_sheet.jpg, ironway_singlet_mark.jpg and ironway_kit_swatch.jpg are sources to trace or judge against: the drafting paper, printed grid, jersey, knit texture and fold shadow never carry into a glyph or the club mark. Glyph strokes and counters are judged in Marshal Orange on the navy of ironway_kit_swatch.jpg, never on white.
